f4b4bb981e:140e76cbca592c2f.title: BAROQUE BIOLOGY
f4b4bb981e:140e76cbca592c2f.summary: If you closely observe the genetics of any living being, you'll see everything is much more baroque than functional. Midway between perfecting and contaminating, aesthetics refuse to be domesticated. Biology, like creativity, is immensely messy, caught in the constant cycle of decay, regeneration and return. Baroque Biology is a curated selection of Alex Valentina's works that explores these primordial concepts. Like remnants found on a beach, the elements in all these pieces carry the scent of the sea and subsoil ? rarities like pearls and strange shells that appear precious to the human eye, yet are merely discarded matter to nature. Like an island left to its own flow, here the aesthetics of decomposing natural elements speak of life and regeneration, as if each new idea breathes fresh life into all those that came before it. Biological creativity will endure, no matter what happens.

f4b4bb981e:04747559c4c0f482.title: SKELTCH Business Stationery
f4b4bb981e:04747559c4c0f482.summary: SKELTCH explores the moment when ideas first appear on paper. The identity is built around a dynamic wordmark that behaves like a piece of typed text, constantly shifting, rearranging and forming new compositions. Its unconventional structure reflects the spontaneous nature of creative thinking, where ideas emerge, overlap and take unexpected directions. This approach became the foundation for the packaging design. A vivid orange palette creates an expressive and instantly recognizable visual presence. The wordmark is enhanced with a dimensional 3D finish, turning typography into a tactile element that extends beyond the printed surface. The result is a visual identity that feels energetic, unconventional and unapologetically bold. SKELTCH transforms everyday stationery into an expression of creativity, where even the simplest blank page holds the potential for something new.

f4b4bb981e:6cdbda89b88fd3e4.title: PARASOMA
f4b4bb981e:6cdbda89b88fd3e4.summary: PARASOMA is a research project we're developing at NastPlas on the body an organism would have if it were formed by two biological systems in a stable association. What interests us is the boundary between them: one region densifies because it has to bear tension, another stretches into a membrane, an interface thickens until it becomes a compartment. We start from documented phenomena (lichenization, extracellular matrix, endosymbiosis, differential growth, structural color) and turn them into organizational rules. What comes out of those rules is speculation, and we keep it carefully separate from what has been established. None of these forms exist, but each one should be explainable. There are 21 open series. Each starts from a hypothesis, carries its own risk and its own palette, and we discard a lot. As the research moved forward, the rules started to feel too limited for a still image. So we developed two applications that are part of the project.

f4b4bb981e:6e7fa253f7cf0c90.summary: The Tartu Punch visual identity lets sound shape the visuals: typography crumples as if hit by a kick drum, patterns pulse with the bass, and vibrations tear backgrounds apart. Rooted in the physical sensation of music?the kind of bass felt through the whole body?the graphic language translates sound into distortion, rhythm, and contrast. This approach carries across posters, merchandise, and stage screens, bringing the same energy to every format. Bold colour combinations and shifting patterns keep the identity in motion, even in print, while distorted letterforms give it a distinctive voice. Music becomes a visible presence, felt before it's even heard.

f4b4bb981e:0feb901cfb361041.title: IT WAS ALL A DREAM
f4b4bb981e:0feb901cfb361041.summary: This artistic project series delves into the exploration of distinct worlds encountered during my recent dreams, expanding upon my imaginative realm and imbuing them with significance through the act of drawing and rendering them tangible in the physical world. This project serves as a testament to the potency of human imagination, emotions, and the fact that even digital abstract artworks acquire profound meaning when crafted from the ground up by a human mind. This is because they inevitably reveal a fragmentary and intimate aspect of my being, simultaneously exhibiting simplicity and intricacy.

a4977d3fa4:6cbdcea98e6e7fb4.title: Clase Azul México and Hypebeast LATAM Raise a Glass to Latin Music’s Most Important Week

a4977d3fa4:6cbdcea98e6e7fb4.summary: Clase Azul México joined Hypebeast LATAM in Las Vegas for Latin GRAMMY Week, bringing its tequila to the platform's second-ever interview suite, exclusive dinner, and viral afterparty. From the suite bar to bottles at VIP tables, Clase Azul helped set the tone for a week of conversations and celebrations.At the Encore Tower Suites, Clase Azul powered the bar inside Hypebeast LATAM’s exclusive interview space. Between a packed schedule of artist arrivals and interviews, including award winners like Milo J and J Noa, the bar gave guests a place to settle in and raise a glass.The main toast came at Hypebeast LATAM’s Zero Bond dinner, hosted by Arcángel, where Clase Azul was the evening’s exclusive tequila. As guests gathered around their tables, the brand became a central part of the celebration, accompanying dinner and the conversations that carried it into the night. Clase Azul followed crowds to the afterparty, with its tequila on every VIP table and raised by Farruko, Kapo, Ryan Castro, and more. The finishing touch was made to take home: custom bottles featuring both the Hypebeast LATAM and Clase Azul logos, gifted to special guests to commemorate the biggest week in Latin music. The bottles became a keepsake from a Las Vegas week with plenty worth remembering. Explore the gallery above for a closer look at Clase Azul’s participation throughout Latin GRAMMY Week. a4977d3fa4:1b6b6dbaf772e88e.title: BEYOND THE STREETS Brings Over 100 Artists to London's Saatchi Gallery
a4977d3fa4:1b6b6dbaf772e88e.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:1b6b6dbaf772e88e.summary: Summary Over 100 international artists, including FUTURA 2000, KAWS and Shepard Fairey, come together for a major exhibition at London's Saatchi Gallery.Curated by Roger Gastman, the show traces six decades of graffiti, hip-hop, fashion and activism through rare archives, historic works and immersive installations. BEYOND THE STREETS has returned to London's Saatchi Gallery with an expansive new exhibition celebrating six decades of street culture and its lasting influence on contemporary art. Bringing together more than 100 international artists and cultural figures, the presentation explores how graffiti, hip-hop, fashion, music and activism have shaped creative expression across generations.Spanning more than ten rooms, the exhibition features a mix of historic works, new commissions, rare archival materials and immersive installations. Among the participating artists are graffiti pioneers FUTURA 2000, LADY PINK, TAKI 183, DONDI and PHASE 2, alongside contemporary figures including KAWS, Shepard Fairey, Barry McGee, Kenny Scharf, Damien Hirst, Jenny Holzer, Invader and VHILS.Rather than focusing solely on street art's visual language, BEYOND THE STREETS examines the broader cultural movements that emerged alongside it. Highlights include "Subway Art," "Tube Graffiti History," "Londonz Burning Archive" and "History of Spray Paint & Infinity Room," tracing the evolution of graffiti from New York City's subway system to London's underground scene. Dedicated sections also spotlight the influence of 2Tone music and fashion, hip-hop photography, underground publications and the evolution of breakbeat culture.Photography and archival materials play a central role in the exhibition, with contributions from Martha Cooper, Henry Chalfant, Janette Beckman and Estevan Oriol documenting the communities and creative movements that helped define street culture. Elsewhere, works by the Guerrilla Girls and archival material from activist collectives explore how public spaces…

a4977d3fa4:e0e197b57f6427a0.title: Zain Memon Designs a Jaeger-LeCoultre Escape Game Set Inside the Manufacture
a4977d3fa4:e0e197b57f6427a0.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:e0e197b57f6427a0.summary: When Jaeger-LeCoultre first teased the idea of making a video game, the response from journalists was blunt. "I got feedback like, 'You're crazy! How do you want to develop a video game?'" recalls Chief Marketing Officer Matthieu Le Voyer. How, critics asked, could a watch Maison hope to compete with Blizzard and Activision? But the Vallée de Joux Manufacture was never trying to build the next Call of Duty. Instead, the latest chapter of its Made of Makers™ program brings video games, often called the "10th Art," into a cross-disciplinary roster that already counts sound artist Zimoun, musician TØKIO M¥ERS, street light-painter Roy Wang and pastry chef Nina Métayer.This time, the Maker in the spotlight is Zain Memon, a Mumbai-born, Goa-based storyteller widely regarded as India's most influential game designer. The self-taught creative is best known for SHASN, a political strategy board game that won the Social Impact Award at IndieCade Europe, and its sequel SHASN: AZADI. He’s now deep into MAYA, a sprawling transmedia universe spanning novels, graphic novels, board games and film. For Le Voyer, the board-game pedigree was the point. Unlike mobile games built on quick dopamine hits, board games ask players to sit with a system for hours, making Memon a more natural fit than any digital agency.The result is The Valley of Inventions, an escape game set inside the Manufacture-Atelier at the Maison's origins, with the player stepping into the role of Élie LeCoultre as he inherits the secrets of the trade. Progress hinges on understanding how watchmaking works: iconic complications and inventions, from the chronograph and minute repeater to the tourbillon, perpetual calendar and worldtime, are reimagined as enigmas, interwoven with puzzles about the Vallée de Joux and the Manufacture's many métiers.The game launches globally today as a free app and web experience in seven languages, before taking on physical form: a city-wide hunt across Dubai in December, an in-store…

a4977d3fa4:2eed5a35f6cfdc4b.title: REO Trucks Unveils the Antithesis of the Modern Truck
a4977d3fa4:2eed5a35f6cfdc4b.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:2eed5a35f6cfdc4b.summary: Summary REO unveils the Runabout truck and SUV lineup.Its utilitarian design prioritizes physical controls, simplicity, and easy repairs.Texas-built models start at $21,500 USD, with deliveries expected by late 2028. The historic American marque REO is officially back, teaming up with Frank Stephenson's eponymous design studio to debut the all-new Runabout range. Powered by petrol, the range consists of the T4X work truck, the T4C crew cab and the S4C family SUV. The lineup is a significant departure away from the bloated, tech-heavy trucks currently dominating the market. Instead, REO is doubling down on a radically simple, right-to-repair ethos, delivering a trio of vehicles engineered to be affordable, easily maintained, and last decades.Visually, the Runabout range grounds itself in its utilitarian aesthetic while still carving out a distinct identity. The upright front grille draws direct inspiration from America’s oldest pick-up, the 1915 REO Speed Wagon, while its broad shoulders and forward-leaning stance are modeled after the American bison. Simplicity and repairability are at the heart of the design. Frankstephenson design opted for standard-size, stacked LED headlights and bolt-on wheel arch extensions that owners can easily source and replace off the shelf if damaged. Inside the cabin, physical controls have been intentionally retained and sized for everyday use, even with thick work gloves on.All three models sit on a shared ladder-frame chassis, utilizing the same wheelbase and front bodywork before diverging into different purpose-built forms. The two-seat T4X features a steel flatbed with drop sides for versatility loading from either the sides or the rear, while the T4C crew cab accommodates five passengers alongside a separate load bed. Rounding out the lineup, the six-seat S4C SUV features the shortest rear overhang of the group and a side-hinged tailgate complete with a fully drop-down window. Committed to their anti-obsolescence ethos, REO…

a4977d3fa4:373973cb1869f69c.title: Nike and Devin Booker Officially Unveil the Book 3 Alongside a fragment design Collaboration
a4977d3fa4:373973cb1869f69c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:373973cb1869f69c.summary: Summary Nike and Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker have officially introduced the Nike Book 3 basketball sneakerThe new silhouette pairs a predominantly mesh upper with a forefoot Zoom Strobel and Cushlon 3.0 midsoleThe Book 3 and its accompanying apparel collection are set to release globally in Spring 2027 Nike and Devin Booker have officially introduced the Nike Book 3, marking the next evolution in the athlete's signature basketball franchise. Unveiled as part of the brand's World of Athletes showcase, the new silhouette continues to operate at the intersection of responsive on-court performance and timeless, everyday style.Created for players who prioritize freedom of movement and a low-to-the-ground court feel, the Nike Book 3 perfectly balances an athlete-curated performance system with the classic, wearable design language that defines the Book line. Diving into the technical specifications, the Book 3 is constructed with a predominantly mesh upper for lightweight breathability. Underfoot, the sneaker is engineered with a forefoot Zoom Strobel unit and a Cushlon 3.0 midsole to deliver a highly responsive and flexible ride. Ensuring stability during rapid lateral movements, the design incorporates a supportive TPU shank, while a modernized herringbone traction pattern on the outsole maximizes grip on the hardwood.Highlighting the silhouette's initial rollout, Booker is introducing a trio of distinct colorways. An orange makeup dubbed the "Sun" serves as a direct nod to the Phoenix Suns, arriving alongside a vibrant "Pink Rattlesnake" iteration. Rounding out the pack is a stealthy black pair created in collaboration with Hiroshi Fujiwara's fragment design, officially cementing a creative relationship that the athlete had teased throughout the summer.The Nike Book 3 and its accompanying apparel collection will release in Spring 2027 via Nike and select retail locations. a4977d3fa4:f07b592f520370ed.title: AAPE Taps LNGSHOT Again for Its FW26 “AAPE UNDERGROUND” Collection
a4977d3fa4:f07b592f520370ed.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f07b592f520370ed.summary: After the first-wave “Urban Roaming” collection, AAPE has unveiled “AAPE UNDERGROUND,” the second chapter of its FW26 campaign. K-pop group LNGSHOT fronts the campaign once again. Known for rule-breaking music and strong individual style, the group brings its own attitude to the collection and reinterprets the brand’s streetwear roots for a new generation. LNGSHOT keeps challenging convention and shaping youth culture, and its fearless energy and commitment to self-expression fit with the street spirit AAPE has always stood for.“AAPE UNDERGROUND” looks to the culture that lives away from the spotlight, where ideas get sharpened and rules get broken. The collection draws on Hip Hop culture, avant-garde experimental design and the nostalgic visuals of ’80s horror, and channels that raw underground energy into hard-hitting streetwear.The centerpiece is a newly designed tiger-stripe camo. a4977d3fa4:19118b3e229519d2.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:19118b3e229519d2.summary: Summary 'Soho Art House' is the first book dedicated to the art collection that hangs across roughly 50 Soho House locations in 19 countriesChief Art Director Kate Bryan wrote and edited the cloth-bound volume, which combines essays, conversations and photographyTwelve cultural figures, including Klaus Biesenbach and Helen Fielding, each pick a favorite work from their local House Soho House has released Soho Art House, a cloth-bound book that opens up its global art collection, which spans more than 11,000 works, for the first time. Kate Bryan, the club’s Chief Art Director, wrote and edited the volume after spending the past decade curating and caring for the collection, and she organized it as a guided tour through the Houses rather than a straight catalog.The book is built in clear layers. Andrew Carnie writes the foreword, and Bryan’s own writing appears alongside essays from Ferren Gipson, Jennifer Higgie, Suzanne Hudson and Alastair Sooke. Photography of the works in place throughout the clubs runs between the texts, showing how the art lives in bars, bedrooms and hallways instead of on gallery walls.The most personal section hands the selection over to outsiders. Twelve cultural figures each choose a favorite piece from their local House and explain why it matters to them. Neue Nationalgalerie director Klaus Biesenbach takes on Damien Hirst, and novelist Helen Fielding writes about Harland Miller. The book also includes a roundtable moderated by Bryan with Soho House founder Nick Jones, Jonathan Yeo, who first came up with the collection, and writer and curator Francesca Gavin, one of its early collaborators.The collection’s approach explains its size. It follows the model of La Colombe d’Or, the French hotel where artists once traded their work for meals and rooms, inviting artists to contribute pieces and join a worldwide network. a4977d3fa4:dc86d3fcad8e54ed.title: Take a Look at CAKE’s Striking Aluminum Triangle Lamp
a4977d3fa4:dc86d3fcad8e54ed.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:dc86d3fcad8e54ed.summary: Summary CAKE introduces the Triangle Lamp, inspired by the audio sweet spot between stereo speakers.The fixture pairs a CNC-milled aluminum base with a 400mm anodized light-diffusing disc.Fabricated by Eddie Olin, the metal features an ice-like finish. CAKE is translating the logic of the listening room into an object with its Triangle Lamp, a sculptural table lamp conceptualized by Eddie Olin. The piece follows the studio’s 2025 listening lounge for Spotify, a space devoted to focused, immersive listening, and borrows its core idea from the same world of hi-fi. Its starting point is the stereo sweet spot, the ideal position where a listener sits in balance with a pair of speakers. CAKE’s concept sketch maps that relationship as an equilateral triangle, with the two speakers forming its upper corners and the listener at the point below, and that geometry is carried directly into the lamp’s form.The base is a tall triangular prism milled from a solid billet of 6082-T6 aluminum, its top hollowed out to cradle a 5 W, 2700 K GU10 LED reflector lamp. Instead of shining outward, the bulb throws its light up onto a 400mm anodized aluminum disc, just 2.5 mm thick, which spreads a warm, diffused glow across its surface. The disc is carried on a 150 mm threaded aluminum stem and a coin-slot joint, which allows it to sit at a tilted angle above the base, and is fixed in place with countersunk socket screws. The result is a pared-back composition of three elements, column, stem and disc, that reads equally as a functional light and as a piece of minimalist sculpture.Each piece is crafted by Olin in North London, with the solid aluminum bodies finished using a low-grit orbital sand that gives the metal a reflective, frosted quality somewhere between brushed steel and ice. a4977d3fa4:1e35d930b57732f1.title: Yayoi Kusama Sets a New Auction Record as Her 1960 Infinity Net Painting Fetches $14.7 Million USD
a4977d3fa4:1e35d930b57732f1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:1e35d930b57732f1.summary: Summary Yayoi Kusama's 1960 painting No. 3P.B. shattered the artist's auction record with a $14.7 million final priceThe massive crimson canvas sparked a focused four-minute bidding war at Sotheby's New YorkThe historic posthumous benchmark arrives as the art market firmly secures her early minimalist legacy The art market just delivered a definitive statement on the legacy of Yayoi Kusama. On Monday night, the late artist’s 1960 painting "No. 3P.B." crossed the block at Sotheby’s New York, commanding a final price of $14.7 million USD including fees. Offered as Lot 110 during The Now and Contemporary Evening Auction, the artwork officially set a new auction record for the visionary Japanese creative. Standing more than five feet tall, the monumental artwork is a striking, meticulous execution of her most famous aesthetic. The crimson canvas features a dark ground completely enveloped from edge to edge in thousands of dense, tiny red looping brushstrokes.A concentrated, high-stakes standoff on the auction floor produced the record-breaking transaction. The bidding war spanned exactly four minutes and comprised 10 total bids, driven entirely by two top executives representing clients on the phone. Evelyn Lin, the chairman of modern and contemporary art, Asia, traded steady escalating offers against Sotheby's chairman Lisa Dennison. Ultimately, Lin secured the winning bid for her buyer. The intense exchange pushed the painting to a hammer price of $12.5 million USD, a figure that landed squarely inside the house’s presale estimate of $10 million to $15 million.Created in 1960, the painting stands as a pivotal early work from Kusama's legendary Infinity Net series, a body of large-scale monochrome abstractions that radically altered the trajectory of modern art. a4977d3fa4:eb9f9fe79bfb1ff5.summary: Summary Mercedes-Benz is launching hands-free highway driving and point-to-point navigation systems in the United StatesThe SAE Level 2 driver assistance technology marks a strategic shift away from early Level 3 autonomyA pilot program will begin for select California residents in December 2026 before a broader 2027 rollout Mercedes-Benz is launching a pair of advanced driver assistance systems in the United States, rolling out hands-free highway driving alongside hands-on point-to-point navigation. These driver assistance systems are arriving as part of a continuing tech partnership with semiconductor company Nvidia. The introduction of these SAE Level 2 systems marks a shift in strategy for Mercedes-Benz. Three years ago, the automaker offered a pioneering Level 3 autonomy system in the United States, but that feature is no longer available on the latest S-Class. Stepping back from those short-lived Level 3 efforts, which Mercedes-Benz CTO Jörg Burzer described as "early", the luxury marque is recalibrating its approach to automation.The hands-free highway driving system is limited to eligible roads for dedicated freeway use. Operating at speeds up to 85 miles per hour, the system handles highway driving and route decision-making. This functionality allows drivers to take their hands off the steering wheel, provided they maintain active supervision of the vehicle. In contrast, the hands-on point-to-point navigation system handles city driving workloads and reacts to dynamic traffic scenarios in real time. Because both new Mercedes-Benz features operate as SAE Level 2 driver assistance systems, they demand continuous human oversight, leaving the driver responsible for intervening before a problem occurs.Before going public with the rollout, Mercedes-Benz allowed media outlets to test both systems on the streets of San Francisco. a4977d3fa4:3b5f9016fa5728c1.title: How Did A Secretlab Chair End Up in Every Room That Matters?

a4977d3fa4:3b5f9016fa5728c1.summary: Once you notice it, you can't stop noticing it. It's behind Magnus Carlsen as he dismantles an opponent from home. It's under Hans Zimmer while he builds the low, seismic dread of Dune. It's the seat Keith Gill — Roaring Kitty to the internet — chose to sit on, in its Game of Thrones House Lannister trim, as he faced the US House Financial Services Committee. Jose Mourinho plots in one; Kevin De Bruyne recovers in one; Post Malone, Marshmello, iShowSpeed and Max Verstappen have all shown up in the same tall-backed silhouette.A quick search for "gaming chair" pulls up dozens of near-identical products, which is exactly what makes the real question interesting. It isn't why gaming chairs are having a moment, but more of why this one keeps appearing in rooms that have nothing to do with each other. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Verstappen Sim Racing (@verstappensimracing)To find out, I flew to Singapore, where Secretlab was founded in 2014 by two former StarCraft II semi-pros, Ian Ang and Alaric Choo. They were training in chairs they couldn't stand, so they decided to build their own.The problem they were solving was specific and punishing. Competitive players can stay seated for up to 16 hours in a single training day. They swing between locked-in concentration and short breaks, and a chair built for that has to stay supportive through all of it, day after day. That spec made the chair a fixture at major esports tournaments, where pros compete for multi-million-dollar prize pools, and in the backgrounds of streamers broadcasting to millions from their bedrooms. Before most people knew the name, they'd already seen the silhouette.The logic that followed was simple: a chair that could keep up with a pro player could keep up with anyone who spends serious time sitting down. The pandemic put that to the test at scale. When work, school and much of social life moved home, millions of people suddenly found themselves at a desk all day and started paying…

a4977d3fa4:d74b48e1a19b8d5f.summary: Summary One Block Down and Nike unveil the Air Max 95 LUX "Italy" and matching apparel.The premium leather sneakers feature Black, Red, Green, and White colorways.Releases start November 13 at OBD, with a November 19 global launch. One Block Down and Nike have officially unveiled their latest collaboration: the Air Max 95 LUX “Italy”, alongside a football-inspired apparel capsule. Centered on the rich cultural intersections of Italian footwear craftsmanship and the 1990s golden era of Nike Football, the collaboration serves as a contemporary evolution of the original Made-in-Italy Air Max 95 LUX from 2001.Rather than reproducing the original 2001 model, One Block Down opted to elevate the silhouette by introducing a newly sculpted, padded upper that honors the original sneaker while feeling contemporary. Constructed with premium Italian leather chosen for its distinct character, the footwear is available in four distinct colorways: a Black edition pays tribute to the original 2001 release, while Red, White, and Green editions serve as a nod to the Italian tricolor. The latter three feature digitally printed gradients that were developed and applied directly in Italy.Accompanying the sneakers is a technical apparel capsule collection inspired by Nike Football’s heritage. The collection includes a jersey, jacket, trousers, and two skull caps that reinterpret the iconic Nike Football Dorito identity and Total 90 branding rather than simply reproducing them. As a nod to One Block Down’s founding year and its ethos to “give everything from day one,” the Total 90 symbol is flipped to read “09”. Additional tributes to the Italian flag are woven throughout the garments’ construction, highlighted by the contrast stitching on all garments and an internal tricolor tape featured on the Training T-shirt.The One Block Down x Nike Air Max 95 LUX “Italy” collection launches on November 13. a4977d3fa4:970b3666284d0c33.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:970b3666284d0c33.summary: Summary SEGA’s Stranger Than Heaven drops its “Act 2: Kure” story trailer.The prequel explores Makoto Daito’s 1929 yakuza rise in Hiroshima.The preview highlights brutal combat, sword clashes, and heavy emotional stakes. mineSEGA and Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio (RGG) have released the second story trailer for Stranger Than Heaven, moving Makoto Daito’s saga from Kokura in 1915 to Kure, Hiroshima, in 1929. The new footage opens with Daito trying to get close to Genzo Iwaki, the “Emperor of Kure,” and being surrounded by Iwaki’s guards before he is granted an audience. A key moment shows Daito accepting a ceremonial sake cup from Iwaki, sealing his entry into the yakuza after an attack on the family’s patriarch.From there, his new role takes shape: he oversees the city’s gambling halls and collects debts owed to the clan. The game follows Daito across five eras and five cities between 1915 and 1965. Its settings include Kokura, Fukuoka; Kure; Minami, Osaka; Atami, Shizuoka; and Kamurocho, the fictional Tokyo district that anchors the studio’s earlier games. The Act 2 trailer follows an earlier “Act 1: Kokura” story trailer, and SEGA has said more are on the way, each covering a different chapter of Daito’s life. Yū Shirota leads the cast as Daito, joined by Snoop Dogg as Orpheus and Tori Kelly as Suzy Day. a4977d3fa4:4c8f70baf9ad80c1.title: Slate Auto Is Selling a $30 USD “Screenless GPS” That Is Actually a Rand McNally Road Atlas
a4977d3fa4:4c8f70baf9ad80c1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:4c8f70baf9ad80c1.summary: Summary Slate Auto is offering a limited-edition $30 USD "Screenless GPS" that is actually a branded Rand McNally Road AtlasThe accessory is marketed for the company's upcoming electric Truck, which features an intentionally analog, screen-free cabinStarting under $25,000, the minimalist EV relies on driver smartphones rather than built-in displays for navigation and entertainment Slate Auto introduced a limited-edition accessory on its online store, offering a "Screenless GPS" for $30. Instead of a high-tech routing gadget, the product is a physical, Slate-branded Rand McNally Road Atlas. Designed as a companion for the open road, the physical atlas contains comprehensive maps covering the United States, Canada and Mexico.The paper atlas is marketed specifically for the company's new electric vehicle, the Truck. Scheduled to launch in the back half of the 2020s, the Slate Truck lacks a central screen and digital bloat, embracing a minimalist design language. Drivers navigate a cabin featuring manual hand-crank windows and no traditional carpeting. Slate built the vehicle with the expectation that owners will mount their own smartphones to handle navigation and entertainment needs.The "Screenless GPS" highlights the automaker's back-to-basics design, offering a physical map instead of a glowing central infotainment hub. While a standard, unbranded version of the Rand McNally atlas sells for $19.99 USD on Amazon, the Slate-stamped edition carries a premium markup typical of exclusive automotive merchandise.Beyond the paper maps and hand-crank windows, the core specifications of the Slate Truck remain straightforward. The vehicle achieves an electric driving range of 205 miles on a single charge and comes in three distinct, customizable body styles. Starting prices range from just under $25,000 USD to just over $32,000 USD . Preorders for Slate products are live on the company's website as delivery windows fill up. a4977d3fa4:5b0bab89081f0851.title: Netflix’s 'Magic: The Gathering' Animated Series, 'Planeswalker,' Is Officially Coming in 2027

a4977d3fa4:5b0bab89081f0851.summary: Summary Netflix drops a sneak peek for the reworked animated series debuting in 2027Roy Graham confirms the highly anticipated adaptation is officially titled PlaneswalkerThe release puts an end to a chaotic seven-year development cycle following a ground-up rework After years of false starts and behind-the-scenes silence, the multiverse is finally opening up. Netflix dropped a sneak peek video officially announcing that the long-awaited animated adaptation of the iconic card game is set to debut in 2027. Officially titled Magic The Gathering: Planeswalker, the series arrives with a heavy burden of expectation, prompting the franchise’s brass to address the fanbase directly. Roy Graham, the Head of Story at Magic: The Gathering, introduced the teaser video with a mix of relief and reassurance, stating, "It’s really happening. I promise. For real." That self-aware introduction directly addresses the heavy skepticism surrounding a project that has been largely theoretical for the better part of a decade.The 2027 debut of Planeswalker resolves an exhausting seven-year development cycle that saw the property pushed to the brink of cancellation. An animated Magic: The Gathering series was first teased in 2019. That original version was initially helmed by Joe and Anthony Russo, carrying heavy prestige before the highly publicized project fell apart. For years, the property sat in limbo until Netflix confirmed in 2024 that it still planned to adapt the game, though the streaming giant mandated reworking the series entirely from the ground up. This creative reboot marks a fresh attempt to adapt the tabletop franchise after years of production uncertainty.The November announcement video included a sneak peek of the show that highlights why the studio opted for a complete creative overhaul. a4977d3fa4:9987d65faa13cc9f.title: Sony Patents a PlayStation Controller That Lets You Tap a Card or Phone to Pay for Games
a4977d3fa4:9987d65faa13cc9f.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:9987d65faa13cc9f.summary: Summary Sony filed a 2025 provisional patent for a controller feature that pulls payment and login data from nearby smart devices or cards via proximity sensorsThe single-tap action is designed to eliminate manual typing, reducing cart abandonment on the digital storefront while streamlining player loginsA frictionless checkout process is increasingly critical to the ecosystem as Sony prepares to discontinue physical disc production by 2028 Sony aims to eliminate the friction of typing out credit card numbers with an analog stick. In a 2025 provisional patent titled "Video game controller-driven information transfer," the gaming giant outlined a PlayStation controller built with integrated proximity detection. The hardware receives payment details or account information directly from a nearby smartphone or physical card, seamlessly passing that data to the console. The controller relies on near-field communication (NFC), a Bluetooth connection or a combination of both to detect a nearby device, receive its signal and secure confirmation before transmitting the data to the console.These information transfers trigger automatically in response to what the filing defines as "an event that has occurred at the video game console." According to the patent’s internal diagrams, console events that prompt a data transfer include purchasing a PlayStation game, entering gift card details or joining a multiplayer match. Users can complete these traditionally tedious actions with a single tap of their device. The inventors purpose-built this method to bypass digging through a wallet or scrolling through a phone to find card numbers. Stripping away those manual inputs eliminates the slowdowns and malfunctions caused by entering payment or login details on an electronic keyboard.The tap-to-pay feature serves a clear commercial objective: streamlining the process of buying games and DLC from the PlayStation Store to prevent users from abandoning their digital shopping carts. a4977d3fa4:7fe00ffc9be21c31.title: Bryson DeChambeau Is Bringing a Massive Golf Course to Clovis, California
a4977d3fa4:7fe00ffc9be21c31.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7fe00ffc9be21c31.summary: Summary Bryson DeChambeau and Cook Land Company have announced plans to build an 18-hole championship golf course and residential community in Clovis, CaliforniaThe proposed project known as The Orchard Golf Club will be situated on the historic McFarlane Ranch property located in the Central ValleyDesign plans include surrounding every hole with a different variety of fruit or nut tree as a nod to the local farming industry Professional golfer Bryson DeChambeau has officially unveiled plans for The Orchard Golf Club, marking the two-time U.S. Open champion's first foray into golf course design. Teaming up with real estate developer Cook Land Company, the athlete aims to build an 18-hole championship course and a sprawling residential community in his hometown of Clovis, California. The "mega" project is set to be developed on the historic McFarlane Ranch, a site that has operated for three generations cultivating crops like citrus and almonds.Driven by a desire to give back to the region where he grew up and attended Clovis East High School, DeChambeau envisions the project as a community-oriented destination. In a distinct nod to the Central Valley’s rich agricultural roots, the proposed course design will feature a different variety of fruit or nut tree surrounding each of the 18 holes. The massive development is projected to bring significant growth to the area, with DeChambeau estimating it could increase the city's 120,000-resident population by up to 30 percent.While a specific co-architect has not yet been named to assist with the technical design elements, plans for the site have been actively discussed since 2022. The ambitious endeavor still requires final approval from the City of Clovis and Fresno County, with the complex regulatory process expected to take approximately 18 months to navigate. To extend the celebration to the public, the collaborators are releasing exactly ten Kith for PROLETA RE ART Classic Logo Hoodies to the market, alongside flagship-exclusive Wallabees for Tokyo, Osaka, Manhattan, Paris, and London. Each flagship location will receive its own dedicated colorway crafted from custom recycled fabric.Handmade by PROT and master embroiderer E in their Tokyo atelier, the footwear project took nearly three years to complete. a4977d3fa4:f0b76b1d721fb53c.title: Apple and Hebru Brantley Celebrate Creativity in Holiday Short Film 'The Dreamer'
a4977d3fa4:f0b76b1d721fb53c.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f0b76b1d721fb53c.summary: Summary Apple has released a new holiday short film titled 'The Dreamer' to promote the new MacBook NeoThe visual features original artwork created by Chicago-born visual artist Hebru BrantleyDirected by Melina Matsoukas and shot by Bradford Young, the film explores childhood imagination and parental support Apple has officially unveiled its latest holiday campaign, introducing a new short film titled The Dreamer to highlight the creative capabilities of the MacBook Neo. Released on November 12, the nearly four-minute visual is directed by acclaimed filmmaker Melina Matsoukas and shot by renowned cinematographer Bradford Young.The cinematic short follows the journey of a young boy whose early years are vibrant with drawings and technicolor visions. As he grows older, a world that seeks to push out imagination causes his passion to fade. His creative spark is ultimately reignited when his parents gift him a MacBook Neo, motivating the young protagonist to sketch, create storyboards, and animate an original superhero character.Anchoring the film's visual identity is original artwork by Chicago-born, Los Angeles-based artist Hebru Brantley, who created every piece seen in the short. For Brantley, the project carries a deep personal resonance regarding his upbringing. "Our experiences shape what we create. My mother saw the artist in me before I could see it in myself, and her belief gave me the confidence to explore that," the artist shared in a statement, noting that the laptop serves as a reminder of his parents' belief in his potential. Fans can also view “Creating the Art,” a supplementary behind-the-scenes project exploring the pieces utilized in the short film.The Dreamer is out now, while the Apple MacBook Neo is currently available in Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo colorways. Read more at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:05b709a7001d0898.title: Portugal Immortalizes Cristiano Ronaldo's Legacy With a New No. 7 Jersey Design
a4977d3fa4:05b709a7001d0898.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:05b709a7001d0898.summary: Summary The Portugal Football Association has announced a graphic design update to its No. 7 jersey to honor Cristiano RonaldoBecause FIFA regulations prevent the outright retirement of the number, the new design features a small cross on the digitThe updated jersey will debut during the team's upcoming Nations League match against Denmark following Ronaldo's recent retirement The Portugal Football Association has officially announced a design update to its iconic No. 7 jersey, serving as a permanent tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo's storied international career. Debuting during the team's upcoming Nations League match against Denmark, the design shift marks Portugal's first game since the 41-year-old forward announced his retirement from the national team earlier this month.Concluding his international run with a staggering 146 goals across 234 matches, Ronaldo stepped away from the squad on November 5 following a fallout with coach Jorge Jesus. Because strict FIFA stipulations prevent national federations from officially retiring jersey numbers, the governing body opted for a visual workaround to honor the athlete's legacy. The newly updated No. 7 kit features a modified graphic design that incorporates a small cross on the digit, symbolically drawing a line after Ronaldo's historic era."From today onwards, we will have a different number 7 on the jersey, but with the same essence and the same pride, reserving the previous one for the immortalization of a story that will never be forgotten," the federation shared in an official statement. While forward Rafael Leão wore the number during Portugal's previous outing, a permanent successor for the new No. 7 has yet to be named. a4977d3fa4:6133f98f795d6475.title: JW Anderson and Johnstons of Elgin Reimagine Archival Checks in New Coats and Knits
a4977d3fa4:6133f98f795d6475.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:6133f98f795d6475.summary: JW Anderson and historic luxury textile brand Johnstons of Elgin, hailing from northeastern Scotland, have unveiled a new Scottish-made capsule collection.Rooted in an archival check pattern from Johnstons of Elgin, this collaboration fuses the distinct craftsmanship and design aesthetics both brands have cultivated over the years. The three-piece lineup features a coat, a sweater, and a scarf. Entirely produced in Scotland, the pieces combine traditional textile techniques with JW Anderson's signature graphic edge.Crafted from the same raw materials as the knitwear, the coat renders a boldly oversized check pattern in a thick, substantial weave. Cut in a double-breasted silhouette, it features fringed edges that push the rich texture of the textile to the forefront.The sweater reconstructs the coat's striking red check into a three-dimensional jacquard knit. By knitting the pattern on both the front and the back, the piece achieves a beautifully textured finish distinct from woven fabrics. The entire process, from knitting to the final touches, takes place at the Johnstons of Elgin mill in Hawick, a town in the Scottish Borders renowned for its cashmere production.The scarf incorporates curated motifs from both brands' archives and current collections. It pairs a lamb illustration from a 1930s Johnstons of Elgin archive with the Ribbon Anchor that JW Anderson debuted in its Resort/Spring 2026 collection, seamlessly bringing together creative elements from different eras into a single, cohesive design.The collection is slated for release at JW Anderson and Johnstons of Elgin boutiques. Keep an eye out for official announcements from both brands for further details on the launch date and pricing. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:644576658ab7d6f1.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:644576658ab7d6f1.summary: Summary Rowing Blazers and the Grateful Dead have teamed up on a winter capsule of a sherpa pullover and Stealie crewnecksThe fleece’s mountain scene is based on a vintage Grateful Dead tour teeThe Stealie logo is knit in intarsia on a merino wool and cashmere blend Rowing Blazers has teamed up with the Grateful Dead on a cold-weather capsule built around the Clark Sherpa pullover and the Stealie Cashmere Sweater. Both pieces use classic Dead imagery, with the fleece carrying a mountain landscape and the knit centered on the band’s skull logo.The Clark Sherpa is the standout piece, a pullover fleece in the classic Clark fit that runs slightly oversized. Its front has a mountain scenic jacquard artwork inspired by a vintage Grateful Dead tour T-shirt, so the design is woven into the pile instead of printed on top. The practical details are kept simple: a stand collar with snap-button placket, side seam pockets and a 100% polyester build, all in a single Blue colorway.The Stealie knit is the quieter option. It’s a crewneck with the signature Grateful Dead Stealie logo knit in intarsia, which means the skull is knitted into the fabric, not applied as a patch or print. Despite the “cashmere” name, the yarn is a blend of 90% merino wool, 10% cashmere, finished with ribbing at the neckline, cuffs and hem. A co-branded Rowing Blazers and Grateful Dead main label sits inside, and the sweater comes in Heather Gray and Black.The capsule’s taglines explain the mood. The fleece is pitched at Dead Heads of the downhill, an après-ski take on tour merch, while the knit leans into the gentler side of the band’s most famous skull. The Stealie dates back to the cover of the band’s 1976 live album Steal Your Face and has been on Dead merch ever since. Putting it on a merino-cashmere crewneck fits Rowing Blazers’ habit of running cult pop-culture symbols through preppy staples.The Rowing Blazers x Grateful Dead capsule is available now online. The four-piece release opens a multi-year partnership developed with Iconic Artists Group. More collections are already planned.Raw indigo denim forms the base of the debut lineup, and a zip-front jacket and wide-leg carpenter jeans lead the release. Both are cut with plenty of room, while functional details taken from workwear keep that volume practical. An oversized T-shirt and an indigo-washed sweatshirt complete the four pieces.The shapes come from Wu-Tang’s Shaolin references, which pushed the design toward discipline, structure and ease of movement. G-Star worked that idea through traditional Japanese clothing, bringing wrap constructions, the fullness of hakama trousers and kimono-derived cuts into its denim engineering and workwear vocabulary. a4977d3fa4:fc97b453bfcc2cc5.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:fc97b453bfcc2cc5.summary: Summary P1Harmony’s ‘BLOW UP’ debuts at No. 4 on the Billboard 200, tying the group’s highest position yetThe album opens with 45,000 equivalent album units, almost all from physical sales across 30 CD and vinyl variantsOlivia Rodrigo’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love takes a fifth week at No. 1 as Lil Baby’s ‘FRESH’ enters at No. 2 P1Harmony’s BLOW UP debuts at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 chart dated November 21, tying the group’s best ranking on the all-genre albums list. It’s the act’s third top 10 album, and it also opens at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Album Sales chart, the group’s first time leading that list.BLOW UP earned 45,000 equivalent album units in the tracking week ending November 12, per Luminate, and sales did nearly all the work. Traditional album sales made up 43,500 of that total. Streaming accounted for 1,500 SEA units, or 1.56 million on-demand official streams of the set’s songs, and track sales added only a negligible amount. Fans had plenty to collect, with the album released across 25 CD variants and five vinyl variants, each packed with extras such as photocards and posters, some of them randomized.The No. 4 opening ties P1Harmony’s previous high, set when UNIQUE debuted and peaked in the same spot in March. The group’s other top 10 came in 2025, when EX reached No. 9.Olivia Rodrigo stays at No. 1 as you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love logs a fifth nonconsecutive week at the top. That ties SOUR for the longest run among her three chart-toppers. It also gives the album more weeks at No. 1 than any other album released in 2026, moving past the four weeks Drake logged with ICEMAN. Across all albums this year, Rodrigo is now level with Taylor Swift’s 2025 release The Life of a Showgirl, which spent five of its 15 total weeks at No. 1 in 2026. 3664343828:2184eb3b4cc4e99e.author: Alex Tabarrok

d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.title: America’s AI Ambitions Depend on Taiwan
d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.author: Lin Chia-lung
d006da4fe3:eea75378d009c570.summary: The United States and China are locked in a global competition to determine who will dominate artificial intelligence and whether it will be democracies or autocracies that set the standards and values of the new digital age. The United States leads the world in the sophistication and power of its artificial intelligence models, and its innovation base and investment in research and development remain unparalleled.But AI competition is much broader than modeling alone. It encompasses a technology ecosystem that includes power generation, servers, and deployment in real-world applications. Jensen Huang, co-founder and CEO of Nvidia, has described the AI industry as a five-layer cake with energy at its base and chips, infrastructure, models, and applications above it. To win the AI race with China, the United States needs to maintain or establish an advantage in each of these layers. And to do that, the United States needs Taiwan.

d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.title: The New Energy Stalemate in Ukraine
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.author: Tatiana Mitrova, Sergey Vakulenko
d006da4fe3:7c8255a6f6b6499e.summary: Tatiana Mitrova, a fellow at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy and former energy scholar at Moscow’s Russian Academy of Sciences, and Sergey Vakulenko, an oil and gas expert at Carnegie’s Russia Eurasia Center, argue that Russia and Ukraine are locked in an energy war that has become an adaptation spiral, despite growing human and economic costs and despite current US pressure on Ukraine. They observe Ukraine’s remarkable ability to withstand Russian strikes, while questioning claims that long-range Ukrainian strikes will be able to achieve game-changing damage on Russia. Ukraine and Russia have transformed the role of energy warfare in modern conflict, drawing on low costs drones but also new forms of technological resilience that are likely to make wars longer and more dangerous.

d006da4fe3:5ad44315d0de90d6.summary: Monica de Bolle, an expert in Brazilian economic policy, makes an authoritative argument that Brazil’s economic problems will persist no matter the outcome of the country’s presidential election. A Flávio Bolsonaro administration would fare no better than Lula when it comes to reducing debt and delivering growth—and Bolsonaro’s illiberal policies could make the economic picture even worse.

d006da4fe3:d2da9274feed5e6c.title: A Less-Is-More Strategy for America

d006da4fe3:d2da9274feed5e6c.summary: Barry Posen, a professor at MIT, is one of America's leading experts on international security. He argues that the United States military is breaking down because it has been overused and overextended over the last 30 years, and that the only way to repair it is for Washington to exercise much more restraint.

d006da4fe3:e407454ddc8200e6.title: How Russia Sees the World Now

d006da4fe3:e407454ddc8200e6.summary: Dmitry Adamsky, an expert on Russian security and Russian nuclear deterrence strategy at Harvard and Reichman Universities, examines a large-scale shift in Russia’s strategic thinking over the past year, centered around the view that Europe, rather than the United States, is now Russia’s primary geopolitical rival and adversary, and looking at the consequences of this shift for US efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.title: AI Is a Choice
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.author: Alex Imas, Mohamed A. El-Erian, James Manyika
d006da4fe3:f2fe497a723c80df.summary: Alex Imas, Mohamed El-Erian, and James Manyika, leading voices at the intersection of business and technology, argue that realizing AI’s potential requires giving workers, communities, AI labs, infrastructure developers, and big companies a share of the gains. Using insights from game theory, they argue that increased cooperation can make AI work for all.

d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.title: The China Price
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.author: Zongyuan Zoe Liu
d006da4fe3:26bb42beb62831bc.summary: In 1971, as the international monetary system was on the brink of collapse, U.S. Treasury Secretary John Connally told a group of worried European finance ministers that the dollar was “our currency, but your problem.” The dollar had become that system’s official reserve currency in 1944, under the Bretton Woods agreement, making signatories subject to the whims of U.S. monetary policy. Even after Bretton Woods collapsed and many currencies floated freely, the dollar continued to dominate. In the last half century, U.S. currency power has only expanded, as more countries have integrated into the global economy and therefore grown to depend on the dollar. China, reliant on export-driven growth, is foremost among them.

d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.title: Empires of AI
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.author: Niall Ferguson, Lisa Klaassen, Eric Schmidt
d006da4fe3:8d3c26580c9ed628.summary: In this essay, Niall Ferguson, one of the world’s foremost experts on imperial history, teams up the former CEO of Google, Eric Schmidt, and the researcher Lisa Klaasen to make the provocative argument that AI is an inherently “imperial technology”—and to reveal what the fate of past empires might say about the future of U.S.-Chinese competition in a world shaped by AI.

d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.title: “Earth Satellites and Foreign Policy”
d006da4fe3:33fc15a61a4dba01.summary: The advent of a new technology invariably comes with strategic implications, raising the question of who will benefit and whether risks can be managed. In 1957, following the Soviet Sputnik launch, U.S. policymakers and analysts recognized that the satellite, as the American physicist and engineer Lloyd Berkner observed in these pages, would bring transformative effects. The United States could not risk losing out, Berkner argued, but nor should governments allow geopolitical tensions to prevent the technology’s broad benefits from emerging.

d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.title: Europe’s Credibility Gap
d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.author: Claas Mertens, Ngaire Woods
d006da4fe3:9729d1ab8b25d3aa.summary: Ngaire Woods, Dean of Oxford’s Blavatnik School of Government, Claas Mertens, also at Oxford, have written a piece arguing that Europe, despite its attempts at self-sufficiency, remains dependent on an unpredictable United States. The continent needs to address this vulnerability so that it can convince other countries, many of which find themselves similarly vulnerable to great-power coercion, that it is a worthy partner.

d006da4fe3:09191e7fdf89ba60.title: A Better “America First”

d006da4fe3:09191e7fdf89ba60.summary: Charles Kupchan, who served in the Clinton and Obama administrations, argues that many aspects of Trump's foreign policy are worth keeping and align with changes in the international system. He explains how the next president can marry the good impulses of "America first" with the best of liberal internationalism.

d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.title: The Axis of Upheaval Goes to War
d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.author: Andrea Kendall-Taylor, Richard Fontaine
d006da4fe3:daabdb8037186d1e.summary: Andrea Kendall-Taylor and Richard Fontaine, former members of the National Security Council, argue that the members of what they call the “axis of upheaval”—Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea—are deepening their cooperation. Meanwhile, Washington is creating friction with many of its own partnerships. If these developments continue unabated, the United States will squander the strength of its network just as its adversaries learn to make the most of theirs.

d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.title: The Nuclear Deal That Could Save NATO
d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.author: Ivo H. Daalder
d006da4fe3:960aafc689650ffc.summary: Former U.S. NATO ambassador Ivo Daalder argues that the scramble to shore up Europe's conventional defense risks overlooking the continent's greatest security weakness: nuclear deterrence. Europe knows it can't fully trust Washington's guarantee anymore. But he lays out a middle path between dependence and nuclearization that would extend France's and the United Kingdom's nuclear umbrella—a course, he argues, that could even repair the transatlantic alliance.

fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.title: Intangible Capital as a Source of Economic Growth and Productivity: A Literature Review and Policy Guidelines
fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.author: Rouvinen, Petri
fc066e842d:33b974b735b72e1c.summary: Abstract This review synthesizes the latest scholarly evidence on intangible capital. Drawing on 60 recent studies across macro, meso, and micro levels (anchored by firm-level data from Finland, broader Europe, the US, and Asia) it demonstrates that intangible investments have emerged as the preeminent engine of economic growth, competitiveness, and productivity. The literature yields three critical imperatives for public policy. First, the measurement and statistical tracking of intangibles require a fundamental overhaul; at present, a swath of these investments remains invisible in official data and absent from corporate balance sheets. Second, policymakers must broaden their horizons beyond narrow research and development (R&D) subsidies. Modern innovation policy must embrace the full spectrum of intangible assets – spanning software, data, organizational capital, management capabilities, and brand equity –, while capitalizing on the vital synergies between them. Third, the scalable nature of intangible capital demands a synchronized approach to competition policy, innovation strategy, and corporate finance. Authorities must strike a delicate balance: cultivating the incentives and finance necessary to fuel intangible investments, while simultaneously preventing harmful market concentration and fostering broad diffusion of knowledge.

fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.title: Economists, Economic Knowledge, and Central Banks
fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.author: Juan Acosta
fc066e842d:ab0dcab8e5d42453.summary: What do economists do in central banks? Why do central banks hire economists? This book investigates the evolving role of economists and economic knowledge within central banks, arguing that their current centrality is neither self-evident nor historically inevitable. While the presence and influence of economists in central banks today may seem natural, this book shows that it is the result of a complex, gradual, and uneven historical process shaped by institutional structures, disciplinary transformations, and shifting relationships between science and policy. Drawing on a rich but dispersed body of literature, the book traces how economists progressively gained authority through the establishment of statistics departments, the adoption of macroeconometric models, and the emergence of a shared cognitive infrastructure between academia and central banks. Rather than focusing on individuals or doctrines, it examines general trends and institutional shifts across a series of national case studies to show how central banks function as boundary organizations, at the intersection of policy and science.

fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.title: Known Unknowns: Knowledge, Confidence, and Public Opinion on Water Reuse
fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.author: Marco Dâ€™Errico
fc066e842d:61d4ea428c9550d8.summary: Public acceptance can constrain treated-wastewater reuse, but less is known about whether citizens provide a substantive view at all. An influential account of opposition to contested technologies predicts that the strongest opponents know the least while believing they know the most. We test that joint prediction using a knowledgeâ€“attitudesâ€“practices survey of 1, 069 households in Barbados. The survey separately measures demonstrated topic knowledge, self-assessed knowledge, willingness to use reclaimed water, and explicit 'donâ€™t know' responses. Among respondents who provide a complete willingness profile, demonstrated knowledge is essentially unrelated to acceptance, whereas self-assessed knowledge is positively associated with acceptance. The predicted knowledge-overconfidence configuration therefore does not appear in this setting. The strongest knowledge gradient instead lies on the response margin: a one-standard-deviation increase in demonstrated knowledge is associated with a 5.8-percentage-point lower probability of giving at least one 'donâ€™t know' response, against a base rate of 22.6 per cent. The relationship reappears in three sectoral attitude batteries and attenuates by about 19 per cent after controlling for out-of-module nonresponse. The evidence therefore points away from confidently mistaken opposition and toward a sizeable group that is less knowledgeable and more likely to express uncertainty.

fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.title: Venture Capital and Customer Capital
fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.author: Amir Sufi
fc066e842d:d765895f74b481b4.summary: Venture capital specializes in the financing of customer capital intensive firms—firms with higher sales and marketing expense to revenue ratios, a higher wage bill for sales and marketing employees, and a higher tendency to apply for trademarks—and they do so more than other financial intermediaries. Venture capitalists target high customer capital industries with low knowledge capital but avoid high knowledge capital industries that lack customer capital. Firms tilt investment toward customer capital leading up to the initial venture capital investment, after which their scale accelerates rapidly. Venture capitalists focus on financing customer capital because such investments require tolerance for substantial risks of failure in pursuit of extreme upside potential, as characterized by power law returns. This return profile fits customer capital investments more closely than investments in knowledge capital. Venture capitalists that sprinkle small investments across a large number of firms, colloquially referred to as the “spray and pray” strategy, target customer capital industries for investment, whereas venture capitalists that commit larger amounts to a small number of firms target knowledge capital industries. The venture capital focus on customer capital reflects a shift away from its traditional focus on knowledge capital intensive firms over the past 30 years.

fc066e842d:d77e3040274eaa10.title: From Balanced Growth to Innovation Cycles: A Solow-Type Semi-Endogenous Growth Model
fc066e842d:d77e3040274eaa10.author: Thi Kim Cuong Pham
fc066e842d:d77e3040274eaa10.summary: We develop a growth model with an R&D sector in which the elasticity of innovation with respect to existing knowledge can be negative. We investigate the existence and uniqueness of a balanced growth path (BGP) and derive closed-form growth factors, showing that productivity and output growth are semi-endogenous and population-driven. We also establish the global stability under a general production function. Under testable parameter restrictions, the economy converges to the BGP. However, when the knowledge elasticity is sufficiently low, a Jacobian-based condition implies instability, and an N-period innovation cycle can emerge. Comparative statics are conducted to explore the impact of several factors, including research efficiency, input elasticity, and population growth. Numerical simulations map out transitions and mark the points at which stability is lost. They make clear when innovation frictions endanger balanced growth and provide practical guidance for R&D and demographic policy.

5b51167fb0:0132a15a91a18b86.title: The Returns to Government R&D: Evidence from US Appropriations Shocks
5b51167fb0:0132a15a91a18b86.author: info@aeaweb.org (Andrew J. Fieldhouse1 and Karel Mertens2 1 Mays Business School, Texas A&M University (email: afieldhouse@mays.tamu.edu) 2 Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, CEPR (email:…
5b51167fb0:0132a15a91a18b86.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 3959-4002 Abstract Based on a narrative classification of all significant postwar changes in R&D appropriations for five major federal agencies, we find that an increase in nondefense R&D appropriations leads to increases in various measures of innovative activity and higher business-sector productivity in the long run. We structurally estimate the production function elasticity of nondefense government R&D capital using the SP-IV methodology of Lewis and Mertens (2024) and obtain implied returns of 140 to 210 percent over the postwar period. The estimates indicate that government-funded R&D accounts for one-fifth of business-sector TFP growth since WWII and imply substantial underfunding of nondefense R&D. (JEL D24, E23, H50, O31, O33, O38)

5b51167fb0:c7fa8e0ff8b591f9.title: The Unequal Economic Consequences of Carbon Pricing
5b51167fb0:c7fa8e0ff8b591f9.author: info@aeaweb.org (Diego R. Känzig1 1 Northwestern University, CEPR, and NBER (email: dkaenzig@northwestern.edu))
5b51167fb0:c7fa8e0ff8b591f9.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4003-4040 Abstract This paper studies the economic impacts of carbon pricing. Exploiting institutional features of the European carbon market and high-frequency data, I identify carbon policy shocks and trace their dynamic effects. A restrictive carbon policy shock raises energy prices, reduces emissions, spurs green innovation, but decreases economic activity—disproportionately burdening poorer households. Not only are the poor more affected because of their higher energy spending, but they also experience larger income losses. These indirect, general equilibrium effects via income and employment play an important role in the transmission of carbon pricing policies, accounting for about two-thirds of the aggregate consumption response. (JEL E23, E24, O44, Q41, Q54, Q55, Q58)

5b51167fb0:e824f86123436e63.title: Residential Segregation and Unequal Access to Local Public Services in India: Evidence from 1.5 Million Neighborhoods
5b51167fb0:e824f86123436e63.author: info@aeaweb.org (Sam Asher1, Kritarth Jha2, Paul Novosad2, Anjali Adukia2 and Brandon Tan3 1 Imperial College London (email: sam.asher@imperial.ac.uk) 2 Development Data Lab (email:…
5b51167fb0:e824f86123436e63.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4041-4076 Abstract We study residential segregation and access to public services across 1.5 million urban and rural neighborhoods in India. Muslim and Scheduled Caste segregation in India is high by global standards and only slightly lower than Black-White segregation in the United States. Within cities, public facilities and infrastructure are systematically less available in Muslim and Scheduled Caste neighborhoods. Nearly all regressive allocation is across neighborhoods within cities—at the most informal and least studied form of government. These inequalities are not visible in the aggregate data typically used for research and policy. (JEL H76, J15, O15, O17, O18, R23)

5b51167fb0:ed6f6ae7997930cd.title: Durables and the Marginal Propensity to Spend
5b51167fb0:ed6f6ae7997930cd.author: info@aeaweb.org (Nathan Zorzi1 and Martin Beraja2 1 Dartmouth (email: Nathan.G.Zorzi@dartmouth.edu) 2 UC Berkeley and NBER (email: maberaja@berkeley.edu))
5b51167fb0:ed6f6ae7997930cd.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4077-4115 Abstract Durables represent a large share of households' marginal propensity to spend (MPX). We develop a quantitative model of spending that takes durables into account and matches a rich set of empirical regularities simultaneously. Scaling the response of nondurables provides a poor approximation of the MPX on durables when it comes to its distribution in the population, its persistence over time, and its cyclicality. As an application, we study how the MPX varies with the size of stimulus checks and find that it declines more slowly compared to a model of purely nondurable spending. (JEL D11, E21, E32, E62, G51)

5b51167fb0:3196e21e18145698.title: Union Bargaining Power and the Amenity-Wage Trade-Off
5b51167fb0:3196e21e18145698.author: info@aeaweb.org (Lorenzo Lagos1 1 Brown University, NBER, and IZA (email: lorenzo_lagos@brown.edu))
5b51167fb0:3196e21e18145698.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4116-4157 Abstract This paper studies how collective bargaining affects wages and amenities. By merging collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) to linked employer-employee data in Brazil, I combine rich contracted amenities with wage information. I implement a difference-in-differences strategy that exploits a court ruling enforcing CBA continuation (i.e., ultra-activity) to estimate the effects of union bargaining power. Strengthening unions raises wages and amenities without reducing employment—increasing retention despite some labor-labor substitution. A revealed-preference approach shows that amenities account for 45 percent of total compensation gains. These findings suggest that collective bargaining can offset monopsony power, but employers retain the right-to-manage workforce composition. (JEL J31, J32, J42, J51, J52, O15)

5b51167fb0:040a01a62b7769bc.title: Inequality and Racial Backlash: Evidence from the Reconstruction Era and the Freedmen's Bureau
5b51167fb0:040a01a62b7769bc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Eric Chyn1, Kareem Haggag2 and Bryan A. Stuart3 1 Department of Economics, University of Texas-Austin, and NBER (email: eric.chyn@austin.utexas.edu) 2 Anderson School of Management,…
5b51167fb0:040a01a62b7769bc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4158-4202 Abstract How do majority groups respond to narrowing inequality in racially polarized environments? We study this by examining the Freedmen's Bureau, an agency created after the US Civil War to aid former slaves and launch institutional reform in the South. Using new historical records and an event-study approach, we estimate the bureau's impact on political, social, and economic outcomes. Vote shares for Democrats, the party that previously championed slavery and opposed Black civil rights, initially eroded in bureau counties, but these impacts faded as federal oversight weakened. Racial backlash emerged rapidly and persisted, suggesting White majorities sought to offset Black progress. (JEL D63, D72, J15, N31, N41)

5b51167fb0:0ad09d14a2108386.title: The Inflation Attention Threshold and Inflation Surges
5b51167fb0:0ad09d14a2108386.author: info@aeaweb.org (Oliver Pfäuti1 1 The University of Texas at Austin (email: pfaeuti.oliver@gmail.com))
5b51167fb0:0ad09d14a2108386.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4203-4242 Abstract The recent inflation surge brought inflation back on people's minds. I quantify when and how much attention to inflation changes and derive the macroeconomic implications of these attention changes. I estimate an attention threshold at an inflation rate of 4 percent, that attention doubles when inflation exceeds this threshold, and that supply shocks have stronger and more persistent effects on inflation in times of high attention. Developing a model featuring the attention threshold, I show that attention changes offer a joint explanation for inflation surges, inflation's co-movement with inflation expectations, and a long last mile of disinflation. (JEL D84, E12, E31, E43, E52)

5b51167fb0:cde519eb240cea67.title: The Causal Effects of Global Supply Chain Disruptions on Macroeconomic Outcomes: Evidence and Theory
5b51167fb0:cde519eb240cea67.author: info@aeaweb.org (Xiwen Bai1, Jesús Fernández-Villaverde2, Yiliang Li3 and Francesco Zanetti4 1 Tsinghua University (email: xiwenbai@mail.tsinghua.edu.cn) 2 University of Pennsylvania (email:…
5b51167fb0:cde519eb240cea67.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4243-4281 Abstract We study the causal effects of global supply chain disruptions by constructing a new index of real-time port congestion using Automatic Identification System data from container ships and a spatial clustering algorithm. We develop a model with search frictions between producers and retailers that links upstream production slack to downstream supply shortages and captures output and price responses to supply chain shocks. The co-movements of output, prices, spare capacity, and market tightness provide novel identification restrictions. We find that demand and supply shocks drove US disinflation in 2020, while the inflation surge in 2021 was driven mainly by supply chain shocks. (JEL C43, E31, F14, F23, L14, L92)

5b51167fb0:e1d96c9b68fa4eb6.title: Firm Adaptation in Production Networks: Evidence from Extreme Weather Events in Pakistan
5b51167fb0:e1d96c9b68fa4eb6.author: info@aeaweb.org (Clare Balboni1, Johannes Boehm2 and Mazhar Waseem 1 London School of Economics and Political Science (email: c.a.balboni@lse.ac.uk) 2 University of Geneva (email:…
5b51167fb0:e1d96c9b68fa4eb6.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4282-4325 Abstract This paper considers how far private adaptation may reduce future vulnerability to climate risks. Using data on monthly firm-to-firm transactions from Pakistan, we find that flood-affected firms are more likely to relocate to safer ground and shift purchases toward suppliers in less flood-prone regions and reached via less flood-prone roads. The results indicate that firms are imperfectly informed about flood risk and update their beliefs following floods. We quantify aggregate impacts using a spatial model of endogenous production network formation. The findings suggest that firms' learning will shape the economic impact of increasingly frequent climate-related disasters. (JEL D22, L14, O13, O14, Q54, R32)

5b51167fb0:f3cbadd0645f288a.title: Reproducible Aggregation of Sample-Split Statistics
5b51167fb0:f3cbadd0645f288a.author: info@aeaweb.org (David M. Ritzwoller1 and Joseph P. Romano2 1 Stanford University (email: ritzwoll@stanford.edu) 2 Stanford University (email: romano@stanford.edu))
5b51167fb0:f3cbadd0645f288a.summary: American Economic Review 116 (11): 4326-4357 Abstract Statistical inference is often simplified by sample splitting. This simplification comes at the cost of the introduction of randomness not native to the data. We propose a simple procedure for sequentially aggregating statistics constructed with multiple splits of the same sample. The user specifies a bound and a nominal error rate. If the procedure is implemented twice on the same data, the nominal error rate approximates the chance that the results differ by more than the bound. We illustrate the application of the procedure to several widely applied econometric methods. (JEL C20, C30, C52)

21113a7a19:ceb8f0e6118ab179.title: Jlateh Vincent Jappah, on the job market--a remarkable candidate
21113a7a19:ceb8f0e6118ab179.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:ceb8f0e6118ab179.summary: Not for the first time, I have a remarkable student on the job market this year, Jlateh Vincent Jappah . Born in Liberia and now a US citizen, Vincent is on an unusual intellectual and academic journey. He is presently finishing his PhD in Health Policy here at Stanford, and has also taken a full load of graduate courses in the Economics department. He is also a physician, with an MD from a Russian medical school. I am co-supervising his dissertation with my colleague Caroline Hoxby. His main project is on the impact of incentives on blood donation in Sub-Saharan Africa. His results are dramatic. Per-diem cash payments, e.g. for transportation, are far more effective and much less expensive than telephone credits or meals for eliciting safe blood donation. If he sounds really special, it's because he is. I'll be happy to correspond with anyone interested in pursuing him on this year's job market.

21113a7a19:2ee7f4f10d726586.title: Human organ trafficking and missing persons in China, PNAS
21113a7a19:2ee7f4f10d726586.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:2ee7f4f10d726586.summary: Here's a study, recently published in PNAS, that tries to very indirectly infer the rate of illegal organ trafficking in China. It's sure to be controversial. X. Wang, Human organ trafficking and missing persons in China , Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 123 (44) e2608464123, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2608464123 (2026). "Abstract The persistent shortage of human organs for transplantation has long been a global challenge. The prospect of substantial profit creates strong incentives for illegal organ trafficking, including murder for organ harvesting, yet empirical evidence remains scarce. This study addresses this gap by exploiting a unique quasi-natural experiment created by China’s organ policy reform. From 1984 to 2014, executed prisoners were the primary source of transplant organs in China. In 2015, the Chinese government abolished the use of organs from executed prisoners, sharply exacerbating the organ shortage. Following this policy change, the number of missing persons rose notably nationwide. Employing difference-in-differences and triple-difference strategies, we show that, compared to cases unrelated to organ trafficking (e.g., voluntary disappearances), the number and incidence of involuntary missing persons plausibly related to organ trafficking increased significantly after 2015. The effects are especially pronounced among individuals with mental illness and in regions with higher transplant demand and greater transplant capacity. Although we do not directly observe organ trafficking, the spatial, temporal, and demographic patterns we document are consistent with the hypothesis that increased organ scarcity intensified incentives for illicit organ procurement. More broadly, the findings suggest that severe organ shortages may generate unintended and highly harmful consequences, even in a low-crime setting such as China. These results underscore the importance of accounting for behavioral responses and illicit-market incentives when designing…

Below are the PNAS paper, the SFUSD announcements, and then some links to the history of school choice in SF. I. Lo, K. Mentzer, M. YahyazadehJeloudar, H. O’Connell, J. Monardo, & I. November 2, 2026, e2524796123, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2524796123 (2026). "Abstract. More than 65 years after the Brown v. Board of Education ruling that school segregation is unconstitutional, public schools across the United States are again experiencing rising segregation. In districts like San Francisco, efforts to implement district-wide choice policies have largely failed to reverse these trends. Since 2019, we have collaborated with the San Francisco Unified School District to design a student assignment policy meeting the district’s goals of diversity, predictability, and proximity.
